title: Require the implementer to self-review against all repository contracts
rationale: The instruction to ignore coding standards delegates basic correctness entirely to later review, contributing to three corrective loops and substantial token use. The implementer should check the plan, architecture, standards, and validation requirements before declaring completion, especially error paths and asynchronous state transitions.
evidence: agents/implementer.md says “Ignore coding-standards documents.” Despite an initial claim of 18 passing tests and Playwright E2E passing 22/22 three times, review-2.md found an uncaught malformed-URL process crash, an untested documented 500 path, and invalid PORT handling; review-3.md found pagehide data loss; review-4.md found a delayed-load edit-overwrite race. run-state.json records 374,196 implement-stage input tokens and three changes_requested verdicts before approval.
proposed_change: Update agents/implementer.md to remove the instruction to ignore coding standards. Require a pre-handoff self-review against the plan, docs/architecture.md, docs/coding-standards.md, and docs/VALIDATION.md, including explicit checks of failure boundaries, documented contracts, and overlapping asynchronous events. Require every review fix to preserve all existing acceptance criteria and to include a focused regression test or deterministic reproduction.

title: Make plans concise, internally consistent, and validation-proportional
rationale: The plan over-specified incidental implementation details and exhaustive visual instrumentation while containing a contradictory persistence contract. This increased implementation cost and made a later reviewer suggestion easy to misapply.
evidence: plan.md calls data/hello.json a JSON file but step 2 and A3 require its contents to be literal raw UTF-8 text. review-2.md suggested either writing JSON or renaming the artifact; the loop-3 implementation then changed storage to JSON, and review-3.md required reverting it as a major contract violation. The planner produced 13,680 output tokens, while the implementer created three throwaway Playwright scripts, ran E2E three times, and reported 34 visual checks for a small hello-world app.
proposed_change: Update agents/planner.md to require a final consistency audit across fixed decisions, file formats, contracts, tests, and acceptance criteria. Instruct it to distinguish normative requirements from illustrative implementation suggestions, avoid hard-coding incidental environment versions or excessive test mechanics, and choose the smallest proportional validation set that proves the user-visible outcome.

title: Require reviewer remediation advice to preserve higher-priority contracts
rationale: A reviewer finding should not offer a fix that conflicts with an explicit acceptance criterion. Reviews should also not approve while leaving a concrete, readily fixable inconsistency in a protected architecture document.
evidence: review-2.md’s store.js finding offered “either write JSON or name the artifact hello.txt,” although plan.md A3 explicitly required literal file contents and the fixed file layout required data/hello.json. The resulting JSON implementation caused the major finding in review-3.md. review-5.md approved while identifying that docs/architecture.md claimed four server-side modules but listed only three; that defect remains in /home/ian/hello-world/docs/architecture.md after merge.
proposed_change: Update agents/reviewer.md to rank the request and explicit acceptance criteria above incidental naming concerns, and to cross-check every proposed remediation against the full plan before suggesting it. Require changes_requested for any actionable contract or protected-document inaccuracy; reserve non-blocking minor findings for genuinely advisory issues that need no code or documentation change.

title: Add a mandatory process-cleanup command preflight
rationale: The existing prohibition was ignored, and a pattern-based kill terminated the agent itself. A concrete preflight checklist is warranted because this failure wasted an invocation and could endanger the factory process.
evidence: events.jsonl around lines 36580–36626 shows the implementer issuing `pkill -f "node main.js"`; the invocation immediately ended with return code 143 and `failure: "pi exited with code 143"`. run-state.json records implement loop 1 as failed with 39,501 input and 27,186 output tokens. The command directly violated agents/implementer.md’s cleanup rule.
proposed_change: Strengthen agents/implementer.md with a mandatory check before any cleanup command: only use a PID captured when starting the process or `fuser -k <known-port>/tcp`; reject commands containing pkill, killall, or process-pattern pipelines before execution. If ownership cannot be established, leave the process running and report it rather than guessing.

title: Document the real browser-automation fallback and server-readiness polling in VALIDATION.md's E2E section
rationale: VALIDATION.md tells agents to use Pi's built-in browser automation 'when available', but the implementer is invoked without any browser tool, so it falls back to ad-hoc Playwright scripts and must rediscover the working configuration every run. This run wasted one invocation on a missing default browser binary and two more on connection-refused races against a just-started static server. Concrete environment guidance turns three failed attempts into zero.
evidence: events.jsonl line 1188 shows the implementer tool list is read,bash,edit,write,grep,find,ls (no browser tool). Implementer session (2026-10-11T20-49-59-110Z_01a12cba…jsonl) line 13: 'browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at /home/ian/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1243/…'; line 15 shows the environment actually has chromium-1228 and /usr/bin/chromium; lines 30 and 32 show two 'page.goto: net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED' failures after 'python3 -m http.server … & sleep 1'; line 34 shows success only after lengthening the sleep.
proposed_change: In the target's docs/VALIDATION.md, 'End-to-End Validation' section, after the existing 'Use Pi's built-in…' bullet, add: (a) 'If no built-in browser automation tool is in your current toolset, script the environment's installed Playwright library. Before launching, check which browser builds exist (ls ~/.cache/ms-playwright) and prefer launching with an installed build or the system browser executable (e.g. /usr/bin/chromium via executablePath); do not download browsers.' (b) 'When validating against a locally started server, poll for readiness (e.g. curl --silent --retry with a short interval, or a loop until HTTP 200) before navigating; do not rely on a fixed sleep.'

title: Require deterministic end-state assertions (reduced-motion emulation) when verifying CSS transitions/animations headlessly
rationale: The implementer spent three probe cycles (~2 minutes and several tool calls) chasing a flaky focus-ring assertion because headless Chromium throttles transition ticks while infinite background animations run; computed styles were stuck mid-interpolation. It only got stable results after emulating reducedMotion, and had to report the animated focus screenshot as 'Not checked'. A one-line technique note in VALIDATION.md eliminates this entire debugging detour for any visually animated target.
evidence: Implementer session lines 22–34: repeated probes of the focus box-shadow return 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) 0px 0px 0px 0px' (transition stuck) at 20:52:43 and 20:53:24 despite document.hasFocus()===true, with thinking noting 'headless Chromium is throttling the transition ticks since infinite animations are running'; success only at 20:54:01 after adding reducedMotion: "reduce" to newPage. The final implementer report lists 'Animated focus screenshot' under 'Not checked'.
proposed_change: In the target's docs/VALIDATION.md, 'End-to-End Validation' section (browser-based applications list), add a bullet: 'When asserting the end state of a CSS transition or animation in a headless browser, emulate prefers-reduced-motion (or otherwise disable animations) and assert the computed end state, rather than sampling after a wall-clock delay; headless browsers may throttle frame updates while other animations run, making timing-based checks flaky. Verify animated states separately via the reduced-motion code path or an explicit animation-disable override, and record that as the method used.'

title: Require the reviewer to trace each acceptance criterion through chained event handlers before approving
rationale: A user-visible defect reached main under an approving review: the Escape (cancel) path shows a 'Saved' success toast because Escape blurs the heading and the blur handler commits. The reviewer read src/app.js (nl -ba in its session) but never traced the keydown→blur→commit cascade against AC2 ('Escape cancels and reverts'), and approved with zero findings. An explicit AC-by-AC trace requirement, with attention to handler cascades and contradictory user-visible signals (success feedback on a cancel/failure path), would have caught this.
evidence: src/app.js:30-34 (Escape restores text then blur → commit() → showStatus('Saved')); runs/20261013-182115/review-2.md ('Verdict: approve, Findings: None'); run-state.json results.document discrepancy (2) flagging the Escape re-commit as a possible AC2 defect only after merge; hello1/docs/VALIDATION.md browser journey step 4 now documents 'the Saved status also appears, because Escape blurs and the blur handler commits'.
proposed_change: agents/reviewer.md: add a requirement that before returning `approve`, the reviewer verifies each acceptance criterion by tracing the implementing code path end-to-end, including chained or cascading event handlers (e.g., a key handler that triggers blur, whose handler commits), and confirms the resulting user-visible state matches the criterion. Treat success feedback emitted on a cancel, revert or failure path as an actionable (major) finding.

title: Extend the implementer's self-review from 'overlapping asynchronous events' to chained UI event cascades
rationale: implementer.md already mandates checking 'overlapping asynchronous events', but the shipped Escape defect is a synchronous handler cascade (keydown handler calls blur(), which synchronously fires the blur-commit handler). Two implementer passes (loop 1 and the loop-2 rework, which even ran a real browser journey) missed that the cancel path emits 'Saved'. Broadening the self-review wording to cover chained handlers and requiring the expected end state of each cancel/failure path makes the existing check actually apply to this failure class.
evidence: agents/implementer.md self-review clause ('failure boundaries, documented contracts, and overlapping asynchronous events'); src/app.js:30-34 Escape→blur→commit cascade present in both the loop-1 and loop-2 implementations (claude-code-implement-1/3.jsonl); run-state.json documenter discrepancy (2) identifying it post-merge.
proposed_change: agents/implementer.md: change the self-review sentence to 'Explicitly check failure boundaries, documented contracts, and chained or overlapping event handlers (synchronous cascades such as a key handler triggering blur, as well as asynchronous overlaps); for every cancel, revert or failure path, state the expected user-visible end state and verify no success signal is emitted on it.'

title: Deduplicate docs/VALIDATION.md in the target repository to reference the root VALIDATION.md
rationale: docs/VALIDATION.md carries a verbatim ~300-line copy of the root VALIDATION.md framework beneath its project-specific section, plus an instruction to 'keep the framework text in sync between the two files'. This is a permanent maintenance tax and drift risk that every future agent must pay; the documenter itself flagged the duplication as 'a maintenance hazard worth an explicit dedupe decision' but was right not to make the policy decision unilaterally. Making that decision here removes the hazard while preserving the valuable project-specific mapping.
evidence: codex-implement-4.jsonl item_11 ran `cmp VALIDATION.md docs/VALIDATION.md` and found the files identical pre-documentation; run-state.json results.document discrepancy (5); hello1/docs/VALIDATION.md line ~10: 'The sections below the project mapping are the generic framework, identical to the root VALIDATION.md; keep the framework text in sync between the two files.'
proposed_change: /Volumes/ExternalSSD/Dropbox/Dev/hello1/docs/VALIDATION.md: keep the title and the entire 'Project Validation (this repository)' section (commands, applicable categories, browser journey, AC mapping); delete the duplicated generic framework (Core Rule through Definition of Done) and the sync note, replacing them with one line: 'The generic validation framework (feedback loop, categories, completion rules) is defined in the root `VALIDATION.md`; this file only records how it applies to this repository.'

title: Instruct the documenter to replace verbatim doc duplication with references instead of sync notes
rationale: When the documenter found docs/VALIDATION.md to be an exact copy of root VALIDATION.md, it preserved the duplication and added a bidirectional 'keep in sync' obligation — increasing, not reducing, documentation drift risk, which is the opposite of its purpose. A small standing rule prevents this pattern from recurring in future runs and other target repos.
evidence: run-state.json results.document: 'generic framework text (identical to root VALIDATION.md) preserved with a sync note' and discrepancy (5) calling the duplication 'a maintenance hazard'; hello1/docs/VALIDATION.md sync-note line; agents/documenter.md currently has no guidance on duplication.
proposed_change: agents/documenter.md: add one rule after the 'Update existing documentation wherever it lives...' paragraph: 'When two documents contain substantially identical normative text, do not preserve the duplication or add keep-in-sync notes; keep the authoritative copy where governing scope dictates and replace the other with a short reference to it, retaining only content specific to that document's scope.'
